sections.h2: Who is allowed to draft a quitclaim deed in North Carolina?
sections.html:
A licensed North Carolina attorney. NCGS 84-2.1 defines practicing law to include preparing deeds for another person, paid or not, so a friend, a broker or a form website cannot draft one for you.

The one exception in that statute covers real estate brokers acting as agents, who may choose or fill in a preprinted form under Real Estate Commission rules, and it covers preprinted residential leases. The same subsection then adds a flat limit: nobody unlicensed, and no website provider, may prepare a contract or deed conveying an interest in property located in the state, or pass on a title.

An owner who wants to sign a house over to a relative should therefore start with a call to an attorney, not a template download.

sections.h2: What does a quitclaim deed actually transfer?
sections.html:
It transfers the interest the signer holds, if any, and makes no promise about anything beyond that. The General Statutes use the word for releases of this sort. In NCGS 52-10, spouses may release and quitclaim the rights each might gain through marriage in the other's property.

A release between spouses has a formality when real estate is involved. During the marriage, a contract or release touches neither spouse's real property unless it is in writing and both parties acknowledge it before a certifying officer. A notary public qualifies, along with court officials, and the officer cannot be a party to the contract.

Ask the closing attorney whether a quitclaim form or a deed with warranties suits your transaction, since buyers and lenders often want to see more than a bare release.

sections.h2: Can a spouse quitclaim a house to the other spouse?
sections.html:
Yes, for property the grantor owns alone, and the receiving spouse takes it. The grantor's own spouse need not join the deed (NCGS 39-13.3). Some marital claims stay alive, however.

  • An elective life estate right survives unless the deed expressly waives it under G.S. 29-30(a)(2a).
  • A claim to equitable distribution under G.S. 50-20 cannot be waived or released in the deed at all.
  • Who keeps the house in a separation is a matter for a written agreement or a court order, which a family law attorney can draft.

Before one spouse is removed from title, read the loan papers and ask the lender how a change in title affects the mortgage.

sections.h2: Is excise tax owed on a quitclaim deed?
sections.html:
Only if the transfer involves value. NCGS 105-228.30 charges one dollar per $500 of consideration or value, rounded up for a fraction, and the transferor pays it before the register will record.

The article sets aside a list of transfers. Those include gifts, transfers by will or intestacy, transfers by operation of law, and any case where the transferee owes no money or property (NCGS 105-228.29). A family transfer with no payment usually belongs there. When a payoff or cash is part of the deal, let the closing attorney decide whether tax is due.

sections.h2: What does the register check when a quitclaim deed is submitted?
sections.html:
Form and acknowledgment. Under NCGS 47-14, an instrument needing acknowledgment is accepted only when it appears to have been proved or acknowledged before an officer with apparent authority, with the officer's signature, commission expiration date and seal shown. The office is not required to rule on the sufficiency of the document or on the officer's authority.

Paper deeds also have to meet the layout rules in NCGS 161-14: letter or legal size, a three-inch blank top margin on page one, legible black print on one side, and the instrument type at the top. A deed that misses them can still be recorded for an added nonstandard charge.

That check says nothing about whether the grantor actually owned what the deed describes, which is why a title review matters.

sections.h2: Why should a quitclaim deed be recorded right away?
sections.html:
Registration is what makes a deed effective against outsiders. A conveyance is not valid against lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered in the county that holds the land, and priority runs by the time of registration (NCGS 47-18).

Suppose the grantor signs a second deed, or a creditor records a lien, before yours is filed. The later party may come out ahead. For land lying in two counties, the excise tax goes to the county with the greater value, so ask that office where to file.

  • Take the signed original with its notary page.
  • Bring the fee for the filing and, where it applies, the excise tax.
  • Keep the stamped copy with the book, page and recording time.

sections.h2: What should I check before signing one?
sections.html:
Confirm who the record owner is and who has to sign. Then settle what happens to existing debts and taxes, since a transfer of title does not by itself change what the property secures.

  • Ask the closing attorney whether the transfer counts as a gift or involves payment.
  • Ask the county tax office for the owner of record and any balance on the bill.
  • Look at how the current deed vests title, including any spouse's interest.
  • If a sale is planned soon, tell the buyer's attorney about the new deed so the title search picks it up.

faqs.q: Is a do-it-yourself quitclaim deed legal in North Carolina?
faqs.a: Not when you prepare it for someone else. Drafting deeds counts as practicing law, and unlicensed persons and website providers may not prepare a deed for North Carolina land. Call an attorney.

faqs.q: Will a deed to my child trigger excise tax?
faqs.a: Probably not, if it is a gift or nothing is paid. The statute sets gifts and no-payment transfers outside the tax, but any payment in the deal can change the answer.

faqs.q: Can a quitclaim deed end my spouse's equitable distribution claim?
faqs.a: No. A claim to equitable distribution cannot be waived or released in the deed. The elective life estate also survives unless the deed expressly waives it.

faqs.q: What happens if a quitclaim deed is never recorded?
faqs.a: It stays a signed paper without protection against lien creditors and purchasers for value. Later recorded interests in the same county can take priority.

faqs.q: What do I pay to file the deed?
faqs.a: A recording fee set by the fee statute, plus excise tax when the transfer is taxable. Ask the register of deeds in the county for the page count and the total.
